title: LIFE-SCI: Prospective evaluation of quality of life, autonomy and bowel care burden before and after elective stoma formation in individuals with spinal cord injury
summary:
People with spinal cord injury often have major problems with bowel emptying. Bowel care can take a great deal of time, may lead to accidental stool leakage, and can strongly limit independence, mobility, and quality of life. When other treatments do not help enough, a bowel stoma may be a possible solution. However, there are still only limited data on how this procedure affects everyday life in people with spinal cord injury.
The aim of this study is to investigate how quality of life, independence, and the burden of bowel care change after planned stoma formation. The study will also assess whether symptoms, care needs, and satisfaction improve after the procedure.
For this purpose, adult patients with spinal cord injury who are scheduled for a bowel stoma will be followed over time. Participants will complete questionnaires before surgery, about three months afterwards, and about twelve months afterwards. The questionnaires address daily life, quality of life, independence, and the time needed for bowel care. In addition, basic medical data from treatment will be collected. This will allow evaluation of how patients’ situation changes after the procedure.
conditions: Injury of nerves and spinal cord at neck level
Injury of nerves and spinal cord at thorax level
Injury of nerves and lumbar spinal cord at abdomen, lower back and pelvis level

interventions.name: Prospective observation of patients before and after elective stoma formation. Adult patients with spinal cord injury and planned elective intestinal stoma formation for treatment of neurogenic bowel dysfunction are included. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years
Confirmed spinal cord injury (traumatic or non-traumatic)
Planned elective creation of an intestinal stoma (colostomy or ileostomy) for treatment of neurogenic bowel dysfunction
Ability to participate in questionnaire assessments (written and/or oral)
Capacity to consent and written informed consent for study participation
Exclusion criteria:
Emergency stoma formation (e.g. perforation, acute ischemia, tumor obstruction) without primary indication of neurogenic bowel dysfunction
Severe cognitive impairment preventing valid completion of the questionnaires
Insufficient German language skills to safely complete the questionnaires
Refusal to participate in the study
